Rent vs Buy Calculator

A rent vs buy calculator compares the long-term net wealth generated from buying real estate versus renting and investing the down payment in stock index funds. Factoring in mortgage interest, property taxes, maintenance, and home appreciation, it reveals your exact break-even year.

Formula and Calculation Method

Real estate net wealth mathematics and the 5% unrecoverable cost rule:

Annual Unrecoverable Cost of Owning ≈ Home Value × (Property Tax 1% + Maintenance 1% + Cost of Capital 3%) = 5%
Net Buying Wealth = Future Home Market Value − Remaining Loan Principal − Selling Fees (6%)
Net Renting Wealth = Future Value of Down Payment Invested + Future Value of Monthly Savings Invested − Total Rent Paid
Break-Even Year = First calendar year where Net Buying Wealth exceeds Net Renting Wealth

Step-by-step financial comparison protocol:

  1. Enter the target purchase price of the home and your expected down payment percentage.
  2. Specify the mortgage interest rate (30-year fixed) and annual local property tax rates.
  3. Input the monthly rent for a comparable property in the same school district and neighborhood.
  4. Set expected annual home appreciation and alternative stock index fund investment return rates.
  5. Analyze the break-even year where accumulated home equity surpasses compounded stock portfolio wealth.

Worked Example and Step-by-Step Calculation

Case Study: $420,000 Home Purchase vs $2,200/Month Rent over 10 Years
Baseline Assumptions:
  • Purchase Price: $420,000 (15% down = $63,000)
  • Mortgage Terms: 6.54% 30-year fixed ($2,266/mo principal & interest)
  • Taxes & Maintenance: 2.5% annually ($875/month)
  • Equivalent Rent: $2,200/month (increasing 3.0% annually)
  • Alternative Investment Return: 7.5% annual stock market CAGR

1. In Years 1 through 3, renting wins due to upfront closing costs ($12,600) and heavy front-loaded mortgage interest.

2. Around Year 5, home equity accumulation and 3.5% property appreciation reach parity with the invested down payment.

3. By Year 10, Buying generates a net wealth of $194,500 compared to Renting & Investing net wealth of $168,200.

4. Break-even occurs at Year 5.2, confirming that buyers staying longer than 5 years build superior net wealth.

Result: Break-Even Year: 5.2 Years | 10-Year Wealth Advantage for Buying: +$26,300

Common Mistakes, Limitations & Practical Guidance

  • Transaction friction (closing costs of 2% to 4% when buying, and real estate broker commissions of 5% to 6% when selling) penalizes short-term homeownership.
  • Renters build superior wealth only if they maintain the discipline to invest their down payment and monthly cash flow differences into productive equity index funds.
  • Special assessments, roof replacements, and HVAC capital repairs introduce lump-sum volatility that landlords absorb rather than tenants.

The 5% Rule: Demystifying Unrecoverable Housing Costs

Financial planners use the 5% Rule to compare renting against buying without spreadsheet complexity. In homeownership, there are three major unrecoverable costs that build zero equity: property taxes (roughly 1% of home value), maintenance and capital repairs (roughly 1%), and the cost of capital (mortgage interest plus the opportunity cost of equity, averaging roughly 3%).

Multiplying a home value by 5 percent and dividing by 12 yields the monthly breakeven rent threshold. For a $400,000 home, 5 percent is $20,000 annually ($1,666 monthly). If you can rent an equivalent home for under $1,666 monthly, renting and investing the difference is financially advantageous. If rent exceeds $1,666, purchasing is mathematically superior over a multi-year horizon.

Mobility, Career Optionality, and Geographic Flexibility

While homeownership acts as a forced savings mechanism through monthly principal amortization, renting provides career optionality. Relocating across state lines for a 30 percent salary promotion carries zero transaction friction for a tenant ending a lease. In contrast, selling a home prematurely within 24 months almost always results in net financial loss due to agent commissions and transfer taxes.

Three Practical Housing Decision Scenarios

Scenario 1: Young Professional with High Career Mobility (2-Year Horizon)

A corporate analyst expecting a relocation in two years considers buying a $300,000 condo. Selling in Year 2 incurs $18,000 in broker fees and $9,000 in closing costs, resulting in a net wealth loss of $14,200 compared to renting an apartment and investing their down payment.

Scenario 2: Growing Family Settling in School District (10-Year Horizon)

A family purchasing a $450,000 home plans to stay 10 years until children graduate. At 3.5% appreciation, the home reaches $634,700 with $148,000 in accumulated principal paydown, generating $262,000 in net equity and outperforming renting by $48,000.

Scenario 3: High-Cost Metro Area with Extreme Price-to-Rent Ratios

In a city where a starter home costs $900,000 ($6,200/mo PITI) while equivalent rent is only $3,200/mo, renting allows the family to invest $3,000 monthly into index funds. Over 7 years, the stock portfolio outpaces net home equity by over $75,000.

Frequently Asked Questions About Rent vs Buy Calculator

What is the break-even year in a rent vs buy calculation?

The break-even year is the exact point in time when the cumulative equity and appreciation benefits of buying a home surpass the total costs of buying, selling, mortgage interest, and the alternative investment returns of renting.

What is the 5% rule for renting vs buying?

The 5% rule estimates unrecoverable homeownership costs at 5% of property value per year (1% property tax, 1% maintenance, and 3% cost of capital). Divide by 12 to find the equivalent monthly rent threshold.

Is it better to rent or buy if you plan to stay less than 3 years?

Renting is almost always financially superior for stays under 3 to 5 years because transaction costs (2% to 4% buying closing costs and 5% to 6% selling commissions) erase short-term equity gains.

Does rent money go to waste compared to homeownership?

No. Rent purchases shelter and flexibility while eliminating maintenance liability, property taxes, and mortgage interest, which are also 100% unrecoverable costs for homeowners.

How do mortgage interest rates affect the rent vs buy decision?

Higher mortgage interest rates increase monthly ownership costs and front-load interest charges, extending the break-even timeline further into the future.

How does alternative investment return affect the calculation?

If renters invest their down payment and monthly savings in stock index funds compounding at 7% to 10% annually, renting often outperforms homeownership in markets with high price-to-rent ratios.
